Tooltip against the yellow hexes — five ways to lift it off

Backdrop is a crop of your own board, so the contrast is the real one. Same parchment, same text in every panel; only the separation treatment changes.

AStronger shadow, no outline

No line at all — separation comes from a deeper, wider shadow. Cleanest, but on bright hexes the top edge still touches the yellow.

BDark halo behind the parchment

A soft dark pool sits under the whole shape. Works on any background because it darkens whatever is behind, not the parchment itself.

CThin ink edge, not black

A drawn edge in the same brown-black ink as the body text. Reads as a pen line on vellum rather than a keyline.

DSmokier parchment, thin ink edge

The vellum itself is older and browner, so it separates from yellow hexes by tone rather than by any border.

E1px pure black

What you just saw, drawn correctly. The hard keyline flattens the torn edge into a cut-out shape.
